# weather-sdk

<!-- Generated by crucible. Change the model or the SDK configuration and regenerate. -->

The Rust client for the Weather API (`example.weather#Weather`, API version `2026-10-01`, sent as `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request), generated by [Crucible](https://github.com/Operation-Leyline/crucible) from the service's model.

## Install

```sh
cargo add weather-sdk@1.2.3
cargo add tokio --features macros,rt-multi-thread
```

or declare it in the project's manifest:

```toml
[dependencies]
weather-sdk = "1.2.3"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
```

The package is `weather-sdk`, version `1.2.3`; code refers to it as `weather_sdk`.

## Create a client

```rust
use weather_sdk::*;

use weather_sdk::*;

let client = WeatherClient::new(
    runtime::Config::new(std::env::var("WEATHER_ENDPOINT")?)
        .token(runtime::Token::fixed(std::env::var("WEATHER_TOKEN")?)),
);
```

`runtime::Token::fixed` sends one bearer token; `runtime::Token::provider` takes an async function called for every attempt, so a refreshed token is used. Methods are `async`: run them on an async runtime such as Tokio. The client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request.

## Call an operation

`get_city` calls `GetCity`. Every operation has a method like it.

```rust
use weather_sdk::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
    let client = WeatherClient::new(
        runtime::Config::new(std::env::var("WEATHER_ENDPOINT")?)
            .token(runtime::Token::fixed(std::env::var("WEATHER_TOKEN")?)),
    );

    // Values from the model's example "Read a city".
    let input = GetCityInput::builder()
        .city_id("c-0a1b2c3d")
        .at(runtime::time::parse_date_time("2026-01-02T03:04:05Z").ok_or("an RFC 3339 instant")?)
        .build()?;

    match client.get_city(input).await {
        Ok(output) => {
            println!("{:?}", output.city());
            println!("{:?}", output.forecast());
            println!("{:?}", output.request_id());
        }
        Err(runtime::Error::Service(runtime::ServiceError {
            error: GetCityError::NotFoundError(error),
            metadata,
        })) => {
            eprintln!("NotFoundError (HTTP {}): {:?}", metadata.status, error.message());
        }
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## Pagination

A paginated operation also has a `<operation>_pages` method returning a paginator (`client.list_cities_pages(input)`): call `next_page().await` until it returns `None`; each page is one response.

```rust
use weather_sdk::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
    let client = WeatherClient::new(
        runtime::Config::new(std::env::var("WEATHER_ENDPOINT")?)
            .token(runtime::Token::fixed(std::env::var("WEATHER_TOKEN")?)),
    );

    // Values from the model's example "List the first page".
    let input = ListCitiesInput::builder()
        .max_results(2)
        .tags(vec![
            "coastal".to_owned(),
            "capital".to_owned(),
        ])
        .build();

    // Each page is one response; the paginator sends `nextToken` for the next.
    let mut pages = client.list_cities_pages(input);
    while let Some(page) = pages.next_page().await {
        let page = page?;
        println!("{:?}", page.cities());
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## Errors

A call returns `Result<Output, runtime::Error<OperationError>>`. A modelled error is `runtime::Error::Service(runtime::ServiceError { error, metadata })`, where `error` is the operation's error enum (`GetCityError::NotFoundError(..)`, say) and `metadata` holds the HTTP status and request ID; `WeatherException` unifies every operation's errors. Other variants are transport, decoding, timeout and cancellation failures.

## Retries and idempotency

Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. An idempotency token the caller leaves unset is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. These operations fill a token: `create_city` (`client_token`). `runtime::Config::retry(runtime::Retry { .. })` changes the attempt limit (3, the first included) and backoff; `runtime::Retry::none()` turns retries off.
